Series::uniform_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::uniform_() const
Series& Series::uniform_(double from, double to) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with an independent value drawn uniformly from the half-open interval [from, to).

With no arguments the interval is [0, 1). Every equal-length sub-interval is equally likely; the receiver’s current values are discarded and play no role in the draw.

Like normal_, this is the in-place “fill this buffer” primitive — the receiver supplies the shape, dtype, platform, and storage. The factory rand is the create-a-new-tensor counterpart.

Half-open means from can be produced but to is (with probability 1) not. Equal bounds are allowed: uniform_(c, c) is a well-defined zero-width distribution and fills every element with c — not an error.

Reproducibility¶

The draw is deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the exact values; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter, so back-to-back draws differ unless you reseed.

Parameters¶

from (double): the (inclusive) lower bound. Must be finite.

to (double): the (exclusive) upper bound. Must be finite and >= from.

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the samples. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity — every alias sees the new values.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver’s dtype is not floating-point or complex

  • if from or to is non-finite, or to < from

Gradient¶

Not differentiable — a random overwrite carries no derivative through the replaced values or the bounds.

Examples¶

Example 1. Default fill from [0, 1). Seeded, so the values are fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({5}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.uniform_();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0.8438, 0.1131, 0.2531, 0.2190, 0.5193]

Example 2. uniform_(from, to) — a large sample stays inside the interval, with its mean near the midpoint.

pluss::rng_seed(3);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({200000}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.uniform_(-1.0, 3.0);
auto v = x.to_vec<double>();
double lo = 1e300, hi = -1e300, sum = 0;
for (double e : v) { lo = std::min(lo, e); hi = std::max(hi, e); sum += e; }
std::cout << "min=" << lo << "  max=" << hi << "  mean~" << sum / v.size() << "\n";

Output¶

min=-0.99998  max=2.99999  mean~0.998608

min is essentially from, max approaches but does not reach to, and the mean sits near the midpoint 1.0.

Example 3. Equal bounds give a constant fill.

auto x = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.uniform_(-2.0, -2.0);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-2.0000, -2.0000, -2.0000]

Example 4. An integer receiver, a reversed range, and a NaN bound are all rejected.

try {
  auto i = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
  i.uniform_(0.0, 1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.uniform_(3.0, 1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.uniform_(0.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN());
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

uniform_: receiver must have a floating-point or complex dtype
uniform_: expected finite bounds with to >= from
uniform_: expected finite bounds with to >= from

For an integer buffer of random values, use random_.

Example 5. Reproducible under a fixed seed.

pluss::rng_seed(100);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); a.uniform_(0.0, 10.0);
pluss::rng_seed(100);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); b.uniform_(0.0, 10.0);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "a == b: " << a.equal(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true

Complex Receivers¶

For a complex receiver, the real and imaginary parts are drawn independently from the same [from, to) interval, so the samples fill a square in the complex plane — not a line segment, and not a disk.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • to is excluded. Do not rely on ever seeing the exact upper endpoint.

  • from > to, and non-finite bounds, are rejected. Equal bounds are not an error.

  • Integral receivers are rejected rather than truncating the continuous samples — use random_ for integer values.

  • Draws are reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call then advances the stream.

  • uniform_ fills an existing shape; rand creates one.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

uniform_(from = 0, to = 1) fills the receiver in place with uniform samples from [from, to):

  • half-open: from reachable, to excluded; equal bounds give a constant fill

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream

  • floating-point or complex dtype only (use random_ for integers); not differentiable; aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • pluss::series::rand / pluss::series::rand_btw: create a uniform tensor instead of filling one.

  • Series::normal_: unbounded location-scale fill.

  • Series::random_: integer-valued fill.

  • Series::exponential_: a positive, right-skewed continuous fill built from uniform samples.
